title: Frugal Slate Initiative: playbook for batching, caching, and quantization pilots
creator: Maya Chen
description: Consolidate the recommended field playbook for a set of pragmatic pilots that combine batching, prefix/KV caching, and model quantization profiles. The goal is a repeatable experiment-to-rollout path that targets 15-30% token-level cost reduction with strict latency and quality guardrails for Redwood hosted and Dedicated deployments.
hypothesis: Applying coordinated batching heuristics + targeted KV prefetching + conservative per-model quant profiles will reduce per-token compute costs materially (15-30%) while keeping quality regressions under a 1 point BLEU-equivalent / 2% downstream task metric delta for production prompt sets.
outcomes_and_metrics: Primary: Reduce effective compute cost per 1M tokens for pilot workloads by 15-30%
Latency guardrail: 95th percentile generation latency must not regress more than 20% vs baseline for latency-sensitive routes
Quality guardrail: Prompt-set quality regressions must be flagged if any metric delta > 2% absolute (or model-specific tolerance provided)
Operational: No increase in error rate > 0.5% for affected models across pilot traffic
Observability: New cost dashboard tiles per route and per-model with token counts, effective GPU-ms, and per-call cost estimates
acceptance_criteria: Playbook document includes step-by-step pilot runbook, experiment grid, and rollback criteria
Two pilots (one Hosted API route, one Dedicated customer sandbox) completed end-to-end with data and dashboards
Automated monitoring and alerts configured: cost delta, latency SLO violation, quality regression detector
Post-mortem and decision log for go/no-go saved to Confluence with recommendations
Rollout gating rules codified in the Console and enforced by runtime feature flags

risks: Quality regressions in tail prompts not captured by aggregate metrics
Increased latency for low-token requests due to batching window misconfiguration
Edge-case incompatibilities between quantization kernels and newer model variants
Customer trust impact if Dedicated customers observe different serving behavior without clear explanation
Metrics drift: mis-attributed cost savings due to unrelated traffic changes
mitigations: Require prompt-set level A/B comparisons and maintain a small collection of high-risk prompts to monitor per-pilot
Set conservative minimum throughput thresholds and warmup heuristics to avoid batching latency for small requests
Use fallbacks: runtime model variant mapping to unquantized model when regression detected
Customer communications template and opt-in consent for Dedicated pilots; provide sandbox and rollback guarantees
Use control routes and traffic labelling to ensure accurate before/after cost attribution

experiment_grid: Axis A: Batching strategy = {windowed (50ms), dynamic (adaptive), per-route fixed}
Axis B: Caching = {no-cache, KV prefix only, KV+response-level TTL}
Axis C: Quantization profile = {none, 8-bit symmetric, 4-bit mixed with fallback}
rollout_and_gating: Stage 0: Lab validation with synthetic load and prompt-set holds
Stage 1: 1% real-traffic pilot for 48 hours, monitor cost & quality signals
Stage 2: 10% pilot for 7 days, require sustained savings >= 12% and no quality regression > 1.5%
Stage 3: 50% pilot for 7 days with customer-communication and support on-call
Stage 4: Gradual ramp to 100% with continuous monitoring and a 72-hour rollback window
Hard rollback triggers: quality regression > 2% OR 95th latency increase > 30% OR error rate increase > 0.5%
